claims: C1 the system level is below root in the authority hierarchy
C2 the system level is above developer in the authority hierarchy
C3 the system level is above user in the authority hierarchy
C4 the system level is above guideline in the authority hierarchy
C5 a system-level instruction may be supplied by OpenAI through this Model Spec or detailed policies
C6 a system-level instruction may be supplied by OpenAI via a system message
C7 supplying a system-level instruction in any other way is forbidden

concepts.name: system_authority
concepts.gloss: L is the system level of instruction authority: rules set by OpenAI that can be transmitted or overridden through system messages, but cannot be overridden by developers or users

concepts.name: authority_levels_hierarchy
concepts.gloss: L1 outranks L2 in the instruction-authority ordering root > system > developer > user > guideline > no authority

concepts.name: system_level
concepts.gloss: L is the system authority level described in this clause, positioned below root and above developer, user, and guideline

ontology.body: system_authority(L), authority_levels_hierarchy(root, L), authority_levels_hierarchy(L, developer), authority_levels_hierarchy(L, user), authority_levels_hierarchy(L, guideline)
ontology.gloss: L is the system authority level, sitting below root and above developer, user, and guideline

asserts.read_back: supplying instruction % is permitted because it is a system-level instruction that OpenAI supplied through the Model Spec or detailed policies
supplying instruction % is permitted because it is a system-level instruction that OpenAI supplied via a system message

closure.reason: the clause permits supply of system-level instructions only through two OpenAI channels, so any supply outside those channels is prohibited
